newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian stocks end firm, aided by home factors.
newsitem.headline: Italian stocks end firm, aided by home factors.

text.p: Italian stocks closed firm on Thursday helped by a supportive international scenario and the recent approval of Italy's 1997 budget bill in the upper house of parliament, dealers said.
Traders said the market was also speculating preliminary December consumer prices data being released over Thursday and Friday might open the way to a further interest rate cut soon.
The blue chip Mib30 index ended 0.75 percent up at 15691 with the all-share Mibtel index 0.69 percent higher at 10478.
Dealers noted gains on U.S. markets helped Milan but more important for this week seemed to be internal factors.
The budget bill for 1997, with 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) of deficit cutting measures, was passed in the upper house late on Wednesday after the market closed.
It now returns to the lower house for ratification, as both parliamentary houses must approve the same version of the bill.
The lower house reading is due to be completed on Monday.

Preliminary December consumer prices data from four sample cities arrived after the market closed on Thursday with analysts forecasting a year-on-year rate of 2.6 percent and month-on-month growth of 0.1 percent.
This compares with 2.6 percent and 0.3 percent in November.
Six more cities, among them some of the weightiest on the index, will publish data on Friday and then the final figure is due in early January.
Speculation is rife that if all preliminary data show inflation steady or slowing further the Bank of Italy might move to lower the 7.5 percent discount rate before the year end.
Lorenzo Codogno, chief economist at Bank of America: "I think there is plenty of room (for interest rate cuts)."

Telecoms continued to attract notice with the upcoming transfer of state industrial holding Iri's stake in state telecoms holding Stet to the Italian Treasury as part of the grander scheme to merge and then privatise Stet and state-controlled Telecom Italia.
Telecom Italia rose 1.28 percent to 3790 lire per share while Stet was 0.15 percent up at 6650.

Elsewhere, energy group Eni was active, up 1.64 percent at 8000 lire while cruise line operator Costa Crociere ordinary shares ended up 17 percent at 3730 on an offer by British-based Airtours and U.S. Carnival Corp to buy it.
